Halden Institute — Internal Memorandum
To: Research staff From: Office of the Director Subject: Partnership review and instrument
standards
Partnership review
The Institute's partnership with Meridian on the Kepler Initiative has been reviewed and the
Director recommends continuing it through the programme's fifth year. Kepler remains the
Institute's largest external collaboration.
Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen will continue as the Institute's co-chair. Staff should route programme
correspondence through her office rather than contacting Meridian's Lisbon office directly.
A note on history
Several staff have asked about the Institute's earlier connection to Meridian Labs. Dr. Amara
Okonkwo led the Institute's sensor group before leaving to direct Meridian in 2021. The working
relationship between the two organisations predates the Kepler Initiative by some years, and the
Institute holds a non-exclusive licence to the Wavelet platform as a result.
Instrument standards
Following the salinity drift reported by the Kepler team, the Institute is adopting an annual
recalibration requirement for all buoy-mounted instruments, not only Wavelet units. Tomas Ferreira
has agreed to chair the working group drafting the standard.
The Institute will also begin logging calibration history centrally. Priya Raghunathan has offered to
share Meridian's calibration tooling, which the working group is evaluating.
Budget note
The Nordic Marine Council grant that funds the Institute's share of Kepler is up for renewal. The
Office of the Director expects a decision within the year. Staff should not assume continuity of
funding for programme-dependent work beyond the current cycle.

props.text:
The Kepler Initiative — Third-Year Progress Report
The Kepler Initiative is a tidal-monitoring programme run jointly by Meridian Labs and the Halden
Institute. This report covers its third year of operation, ending in 2025.
Summary
Kepler now operates forty-one monitoring buoys along the Atlantic shelf, up from twenty-eight at
the end of the previous year. All units are Wavelet platforms built in Tromsø. The programme has
published continuous readings since its second year and its dataset is used by fourteen external
research groups.
Governance
The programme is co-chaired by A. Okonkwo of Meridian Labs and by Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen, who
directs the Halden Institute. The two organisations share operating costs equally. Day-to-day
coordination runs out of Meridian's Lisbon office.
Priya Raghunathan serves as technical lead. Her team handled the migration of the buoy fleet to
the second-generation Wavelet unit during the reporting period.
Findings
The most significant result this year concerns the Cascais Anomaly — a persistent temperature
gradient observed off the coast near Lisbon, first identified by Okonkwo in the programme's second
year. Extended observation has confirmed the gradient is seasonal rather than permanent, which
contradicts the initial hypothesis published at the start of the programme.
A second finding concerns instrument drift. Wavelet units deployed for more than eighteen months
show measurable salinity drift, and the team now recommends recalibration on an annual cycle.
Funding and outlook
Kepler is funded through the Nordic Marine Council, with additional support from the Costa
Foundation. Funding is committed through the programme's fifth year. The partners intend to
expand the network to sixty buoys, contingent on the Council renewing its grant.

props.text:
Meridian Labs — Organisation Overview
Meridian Labs is an independent research organisation working on coastal climate instrumentation.
It was founded in 2019 in Lisbon, Portugal, and operates a second workshop in Tromsø, Norway.
Leadership
Meridian Labs is directed by Dr. Amara Okonkwo, an oceanographer who previously led the sensor
group at the Halden Institute. Okonkwo took over as director in 2021, succeeding Tomas Ferreira,
who remains on the advisory board.
Engineering is led by Priya Raghunathan, who joined Meridian in 2020 from a background in
low-power embedded systems. Raghunathan designed the Wavelet sensor platform that most of
the organisation's fieldwork now depends on.
Programmes
The organisation runs two long-lived programmes.
The Kepler Initiative is a joint tidal-monitoring programme with the Halden Institute, begun in
2022. Kepler operates a network of forty-one buoys along the Atlantic shelf and publishes its
readings openly.
Wavelet is the in-house sensor platform: a low-power buoy-mounted unit that records temperature,
salinity and wave height. Wavelet units are manufactured in Tromsø and deployed by both
Meridian and its partners.
Funding
Meridian Labs is funded by the Costa Foundation, a private endowment based in Lisbon, together
with grant support from the Nordic Marine Council. The Costa Foundation has supported the
organisation since its founding and funds roughly two-thirds of its annual budget.
